description: I am Hassana Abullahi a UI/UX designer, an AI and ML engineer and also the team lead for this project
summary: Microgravity Pulse is a daily health check-in dashboard that helps astronauts assess their own health during long-duration missions. The astronaut logs six indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar, body temperature, sleep and mood) and instantly sees a colour-coded status, plain-language guidance on what to do next, and trends over time. It addresses the challenge by turning spaceflight health risks such as isolation, radiation and disrupted sleep into a simple visual tool that needs no medical training. It matters because on deep-space missions a doctor can be far away, so early self-detection of problems protects crew health and mission success.
details:
What it does: Microgravity Pulse is a self-assessment tool for astronauts. Each day the astronaut enters heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar (mg/dL), body temperature, sleep hours and mood. The app rates every indicator as NOMINAL, WATCH or ACTION using a green, amber and red colour code, and also shows a text label so status never depends on colour alone. Each result comes with simple guidance, such as resting and re-measuring, hydrating, or alerting the flight surgeon.

How it works: Rule-based thresholds based on general adult reference ranges (for example, resting heart rate 60-100 bpm and fasting blood sugar 70-99 mg/dL) classify each reading. Check-ins are saved to a local CSV file. A Trends tab plots any indicator over time with the healthy range shaded, so gradual changes are easy to spot. A Learn tab explains in plain language how to take each measurement and why it matters in space, because astronauts should not be assumed to know how to assess their own health. A daily check-in streak counter encourages a consistent health routine.

Benefits: Fast at-a-glance status, early warning of declining sleep, mood or vital signs, clear next steps, and support for crew autonomy when ground support is delayed or unavailable.

What we hope to achieve: A simple, accessible foundation for crew self-monitoring that could grow into a fuller mission health companion.

Tools: Python, Streamlit, Pandas and Plotly, with custom CSS styling and Google Fonts (Sora and IBM Plex Mono).

Future work: an interactive body map showing the status of each body system, timed reminders for the next measurement, environment modes (spacecraft, Moon base, Mars rover), badges and levels, and wearable sensor integration.

Disclaimer: This is an educational prototype and not medical advice.
